samples.summary: URL path segments are interpolated unencoded (`workspace`, `docId`, `tabId`, cell ref), so a caller-supplied id can traverse out of the intended path and issue the request — with the user's bearer token and the command's HTTP method — against an arbitrary server endpoint. The diff adds `encodeURIComponent` only for the api-keys workspace/key id, leaving the same class of injection everywhere else.
samples.evidence: `base` (line 84) interpolates `this.config.workspace` raw, and lines 215/218/221/299/346/352/358/361/364/370/377 interpolate `id`/`docId`/`tabId`/`sref` raw. fetch normalizes `..` segments per the WHATWG URL rules, so `wafflebase docs delete '../../../workspaces/ws-1/api-keys/<keyId>'` resolves to `https://server/workspaces/ws-1/api-keys/<keyId>` and sends DELETE with the session's `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` (send(), line 137). The same trick via `sheets cells set` yields an attacker-chosen PUT body at an attacker-chosen path. Server-side guards still apply, so this is request-forgery within the user's own privileges rather than privilege escalation — which matters when the docId/tab/ref comes from untrusted input (an agent processing a fetched document, a CI parameter). The diff's own `encodeURIComponent(this.config.workspace)` at line 385 is the fix; it was applied to one of ~15 sites.

samples.summary: An upstream-supplied `error.code` is now forwarded verbatim from every command, so a response body can forge the CLI's own privileged codes — `SESSION_EXPIRED` above all — and a consumer cannot tell a client-synthesized envelope from a server-supplied one.
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` (line 76) accepts any body whose `error.code` is a string and `forwardUpstreamError` (line 224) prints it unchanged, while `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:157) synthesizes the *same* `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED', message:'Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`.'}}`. Before this change only six content paths forwarded bodies; the other ~35 collapsed them to `HTTP <status>`. Now any 4xx/5xx body from a compromised or hostile server (including one named by `--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`) can make any subcommand emit SESSION_EXPIRED and drive an agent that branches on that code into re-running `wafflebase login`, which opens a browser at `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:36) — an upstream-triggered re-auth flow. Consider refusing to forward codes in the client's own reserved set, or namespacing the synthesized ones.

samples.summary: Upstream-controlled text and arbitrary sibling fields are now forwarded into an agent's stderr from every command (up to 500 chars of `message`, up to 4000 bytes of spread body), widening the indirect-prompt-injection / info-disclosure surface — including an `error.command` hint an agent may act on.
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` spreads `...body` (lines 163/167), so any field the upstream attached survives as long as the serialized body stays under `MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY`, and `upstreamDetail` (line 140) now quotes Nest's `message` for every command's failure where ~35 sites previously emitted only `HTTP <status>`. `ApiError` documents `command?` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:30) as a hint agents act on, so a hostile/compromised backend — or user-authored content echoed back inside a validation message — can place chosen text, including a suggested command, into the stream an LLM agent reads. Mitigations already present: JSON.stringify neutralizes control characters/ANSI, bodies starting with `<` are dropped, and both length caps apply. Hardening option: forward only the two documented fields (`code`, `message`) instead of spreading unknown siblings.

samples.summary: Routing the api-keys calls through `send()` adds one more place where a 401 causes the session refresh token to be POSTed to whatever host `--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` names, even when the session file recorded a different server. Pre-existing for all other commands, newly reachable here.
samples.evidence: `resolveConfig` (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:112-130) returns the session's `accessToken`/`refreshToken` while letting `flags.server ?? process.env.WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` override `session.server`, with no check that the two match. `send()` (line 137) sends the access token to that host and, on a 401 under JWT auth, `refreshSession()` (line 94) POSTs the long-lived refresh token to `${server}/auth/refresh`. Before this change the api-keys calls used a raw `fetch` and never refreshed, so this is a marginal widening rather than a new exposure class. Pinning session tokens to `session.server` would close it for all paths.

samples.summary: No test pins behavior for a hostile body that claims one of the client's own reserved codes (e.g. an upstream `error.code: 'SESSION_EXPIRED'`), which is the case that decides whether the synthesized envelope is forgeable.
samples.evidence: The suite covers the 500-char message cap, the 4000-byte sibling drop, non-envelope rejection, and the client-synthesized SESSION_EXPIRED for api-keys, but nothing asserts what happens when the *upstream* body supplies a reserved code. Adding that case would pin whichever behavior the team decides is correct for the forgeability finding above.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `base` (http-client.ts:82-85) interpolates `this.config.workspace` unencoded, and the document/tab/cell path builders interpolate `id`/`docId`/`tabId`/`sref` unencoded at lines 215, 218, 221, 299, 305, 316, 322, 333, 339, 346, 349, 352, 358, 361, 364, 370, 377. The same file already applies `encodeURIComponent` at lines 270, 357, 385 and 396, confirming the inconsistency. I traced taint from CLI args to the URL with no validation in between: cells.ts:20-28/41-68/80-94, docs.ts:156, tabs.ts:78, files.ts:145, notes.ts:116, slides.ts:121 pass user-supplied `docId`/`ref`/`--tab` directly, and no id-format check exists anywhere in packages/cli/src (ctx.ts only does list lookup for `ctx switch`, and `--workspace`/config paths are unchecked). `send()` (line 137) attaches the session `Authorization: Bearer` header to whatever URL results, and `fetch`'s WHATWG URL parsing normalizes `..` segments, so a supplied id can escape the `/api/v1/workspaces/<ws>` base onto any other same-origin path (e.g. the `/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys` management endpoints built at line 385) with the command's method and body. The host cannot be redirected because the URL string is absolute, so impact is same-origin request forgery within the user's own privileges rather than privilege escalation — consistent with the reported `major` severity. This is path/URL injection from unvalidated input, which is explicitly in the security lens's lane, so no out-of-scope, not-present, or already-guarded ground applies.

finding.summary: Verbatim, uncapped forwarding of upstream response bodies now happens on every CLI command — untrusted upstream content flows unfiltered into agent-consumed stderr
finding.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:169-179) prints `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` in full whenever `res.data.error.code` happens to be a string. `isErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:76-85) validates only that one field: everything else in the body — an arbitrarily long `error.message`, sibling fields, a stack trace, an internal identifier — is echoed verbatim. The sibling non-envelope path deliberately hardens the same data (`MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE = 500` at formatter.ts:90 and the `startsWith('<')` HTML rejection at formatter.ts:117); the verbatim path has neither cap nor filter, so the hardening is bypassed simply by including `error.code`. Before this delta only six commands could reach that path; this delta routes ~25 more `!res.ok` branches (docs.ts:80/107/121/139/157, notes.ts:40..117, slides.ts:45..122, cells.ts:29/69/95/147, tabs.ts:20/53/79, files.ts:90/110/128/146, api-keys.ts:22/36/50, sheets-import.ts:91, sheets-export.ts:43) through it. Attack: a compromised, malicious, or MITM'd server (`--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` / config profile is free-form and the URL scheme is not pinned, config.ts:90-94) answers any request with `{"error":{"code":"SESSION_EXPIRED","message":"<megabytes of text, or instructions aimed at the reading agent>"}}`. packages/cli/README.md explicitly positions this stderr line as what AI agents branch on, so the payload lands directly in an agent's context, and it can also spoof CLI-reserved codes (TYPE_MISMATCH, CONFIRMATION_REQ) to steer behaviour. Note JSON.stringify does escape control chars, so ANSI/terminal escape injection is not possible — the vector is content/volume, not terminal control. Suggested fix: apply the same length cap (and a field whitelist of `code`/`message`) on the verbatim path.

verdict.reason: The finding's central mechanism does not exist in this tree. It claims formatter.ts:169-179 emits `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` verbatim with "neither cap nor filter", bypassing the sibling path's hardening whenever `error.code` is a string. In fact the envelope branch (formatter.ts:224-228) emits `safeEnvelope(res.data, res.status)`, and `safeEnvelope` (formatter.ts:158-171) applies precisely the controls the finding says are missing: `code` truncated to MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE=80 (formatter.ts:94,162); `message` passed through the SAME `clampUpstreamText` used by the non-envelope path (formatter.ts:113-126,165), so the 500-char MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE cap and the `startsWith('<')` HTML rejection both apply with an `HTTP <status>` fallback; and the entire serialized body bounded by MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY=4000 (formatter.ts:106,168-170), past which all sibling fields (stack traces, internal identifiers, debug context) are dropped and only `{code, message}` survive — which is the reviewer's own suggested fix. `upstreamErrorJson` (formatter.ts:249-250) shares the same helper, so the import/upload/download io.stderr paths are covered too. Tests pin this behaviour: test/upstream-error.test.ts:130-137 (5000-char message clamped to 500+ellipsis), :139-150 (6000-char sibling `stack` dropped), :152-160 (HTML message replaced with `HTTP 502`). The claimed attack — megabytes of upstream-controlled text or a stack trace flooding agent-consumed stderr because `error.code` happens to be a string — is therefore impossible: stderr is bounded at ~4KB with message text capped at 500 chars and HTML documents rejected. The comment at formatter.ts:96-106 explicitly names the unbounded `JSON.stringify(res.data)` variant as the design that was rejected. The only residual is that non-`code`/`message` sibling fields survive while the body stays under 4KB, a documented and bounded choice, not the uncapped/unfiltered defect asserted. (The sole remaining raw `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` in the package is src/files/upload.ts:221, a success-path stdout write outside this finding's scope.)
